thread.title: The stock market was on the verge of the worst start to a year in 20 years at the lows - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: The stock market was on the verge of the worst start to a year in 20 years at the lows - MarketWatch
text:
Wall Street investors couldn’t part ways with 2018 rapidly enough, but it turns out that 2019 is setting up to be equally ugly to stock-market bulls.
According to Dow Jones Market Data, at Thursday’s session lows, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -2.46% and the S&P 500 index SPX, -2.05% were on track to post their worst start to a year since 2000.
Of course, that only represents two sessions, but it’s worth noting that broader market managed to eke out tepid gains on Wednesday , the day after New Year’s Day, when most major indexes were closed.
Thursday, however, represented a markedly different, and perhaps more dreary, story, with the Dow down 1.6% in recent trade (the index was down 678 points at its lows), the S&P 500 was off 1%, while the Nasdaq Composite Index was down 1.3%.
Read: Opinion: Apple lives up to Wall Street’s fears with massive revenue shortfall
In fact, all three indexes were off their worst levels of the session in a volatile session.
MarketWatch’s data team says that at the worst levels, with the Dow down 2.9%, would mark the worst start to a year since 2000 when the blue-chip gauge fell 4.34% in the first two trading days. The S&P 500, down 2.48% at its nadir, was pacing its worst such start since 2000 when it fell 4.75%.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq’ Composite Index’s COMP, -2.53% more than 2% skid earlier in the session was only its worst start to a year since 2016.
Losses for the equity market were partly fueled by a one-two punch of downbeat news. Apple Inc. AAPL, -9.31% late Wednesday issued a rare reduction to its sales forecast for the latest quarter. Then Thursday morning the Institute for Supply Management said its manufacturing index fell to 54.1 in December, down from 59.3 in November and below the 57.9 anticipated by economists surveyed by MarketWatch economists.
Check out: S&P 500 nails resistance (2,520), pulls in amid Apple-fueled volatility
That data rattled an already jittery market that has been agonizing over the possibility of a recession taking root in the U.S. economy.
—Kevin Jimenez contributed to the this article
Mark DeCambre Mark DeCambre is MarketWatch's markets editor. He is based in New York. Follow him on Twitter @mdecambre.
